text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER #sev1: High error rate observed on /v1/generate for model 'redwood-v2-compat' — spike started ~10m ago. Attaching alerts and traces.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-06-15T10:12Z -> rolling canary to us-west-2 for redwood-v2-compat (weightset: ws-2026-06-15-a). Triggered by release pipeline.

Maria Chen: seeing a 30% 5xx rate on the canary nodes. RTTs look ok, but responses are malformed (tokenization errors) — examples in logs.

Kevin Patel: I can take. Is this limited to canary? Any customer impact?

Sofia Ruiz: Can confirm non-canary traffic still fine. But some customers on canary routing are getting garbled outputs (weird tokens, <UNK> tokens embedded). Panic if they are using structured outputs.

Oliver Grant: I pulled a trace — tokenizer mismatch between model checkpoints. The served weightset references tokenizer v1.3 while the runtime used v1.2. Looks like packaging step didn't include tokenizer bundle.

Jamie Liao: tagging @deploy-bot -- did the release include tokenizer bundle?

deploy-bot: Release metadata: weightset ws-2026-06-15-a, tokenizer_ref: tokenizer:v1.3, artifact uploaded: true. Diff vs previous: tokenizer checksum mismatch flagged in post-upload check but passed a later validation step.

Maria Chen: we need immediate mitigation: abort canary and flip feature flag routing to fallback variant (redwood-v2-stable). Also page on-call for rollback readiness.

Kevin Patel: I'm on-call. I'll flip the kill-switch flag. Which flag name?

Sofia Ruiz: flag is routes.model_redwood_v2_compat.enable_canary_us_west2. To abort: set to false.

Kevin Patel: executing toggle now:
```
# feature-flag toggle
curl -X POST https://console.flags.internal/toggle \
  -d '{"flag":"routes.model_redwood_v2_compat.enable_canary_us_west2","value":false}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

Kevin Patel: Toggle applied. Confirming traffic shift...

support-bot: Routing metrics: canary traffic dropped from 8% -> 0.5% over 45s. Majority of requests redirected to redwood-v2-stable. Error rate on /v1/generate returning to baseline for affected customers.

Oliver Grant: Good. Need a quick customer-impact assessment. Which customers were on the canary group? List from config: beta-cust-9, analytics-labs, internal-ci.

Jamie Liao: contacting customer success to notify beta-cust-9 and analytics-labs. Draft message: "We briefly routed you to a canary model with a packaging mismatch that caused malformed tokens; we rolled back your routing and are investigating. No data loss." Thoughts?

Maria Chen: that sounds fine. Marking incident as "degraded for canary cohort". Start collecting logs and the failing inputs for eval.

Kevin Patel: I'll prepare a hotfix rollback plan: two options — 1) repackage tokenizer v1.3 and re-deploy canary, 2) force runtime to use compatible tokenizer mapping (hotpatch) until proper bundle is uploaded. Option 2 is faster but risky.

Sofia Ruiz: option 2: runtime override is `TOKENIZER_ALIAS_OVERRIDE=tokenizer:v1.2->tokenizer:v1.3-compat` — but that requires a restart of the canary processes and may affect KV cache compatibility. Prefer repackage and redeploy (option 1) as safe approach.

Oliver Grant: Agree. We'll do option 1. I'll start a repackage (locking checksum verification) and add stricter pre-deploy validation to catch mismatched tokenizer checksum vs runtime.

Jamie Liao: ETA for repackage?

Oliver Grant: ~25-30m to rebuild, verify, and stage. Canary redeploy after verification. I'll push artifacts to staging and ping here when done.

Maria Chen: hands off to oncall for monitoring — @Kevin you'll oversee the rollback window and customer comms; @Jamie handle customer messages; @Oliver handle artifact verification.

Kevin Patel: acknowledged. Also enabling extra tracing on redirect path and adding a temporary alert: if malformed-token > 1% for any production route, page.

deploy-bot: Canary abort recorded by Kevin Patel at 2026-06-15T10:18Z. Rollback flag set: canary_aborted=true.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created PD-INC-8741. Assigned to Kevin Patel (on-call). Priority: P1 (customer-impact on small cohort).

support-bot: CS notified: ticket created TKT-3229. Initial customer message queued to be sent after internal review.

Oliver Grant: repackage done. checksum: abc123... Verified tokenizer:v1.3 matches weightset. Starting staged canary deploy to us-west-2 (single node) for verification.

deploy-bot: Staged deploy to canary-node-7 started. Healthchecks running.

Sofia Ruiz: healthchecks passing on staged node. Running a quick synthetic suite with previously failing inputs.

Sofia Ruiz: synthetic tests: previously malformed sequences now correct. No <UNK> tokens.

Kevin Patel: good. Proceeding to slow canary ramp: 1% -> 4% -> hold. Monitoring for 10m at each step.

support-bot: Customer impact update: initial messages sent to beta-cust-9 and analytics-labs advising rollback and mitigation steps. No escalations yet.

Maria Chen: after ramp hold, if no regressions, we'll schedule a controlled rollout. Also file a postmortem: root cause = packaging pipeline allowed tokenizer checksum mismatch through a late-stage validation override; remediation = tighten CI checks + add e2e synthetic on packaging artifacts.

Jamie Liao: noted. I'll start the incident writeup template. Assigning owners: OLIVER=artifact fix, KEVIN=oncall + alerting, MARIA=postmortem lead, JAMIE=customer comms.

Kevin Patel: marking incident as mitigated for larger population. Keeping PD ticket open until postmortem and followups complete.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-8741 status updated -> mitigated (reduced customer impact) at 2026-06-15T11:05Z.

Maria Chen: closing notes: ensure tokenizer and weightset are versioned together in artifact metadata, and add a kill-switch runbook entry for malformed-token scenarios. Thanks team. :tada:
